hero.subtitle: A fall at an Oakley store, apartment complex, or parking lot can leave you with real medical bills and no clear answers. LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles premises liability claims in Contra Costa County.

about.title: Oakley Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Oakley has grown quickly, and with that growth comes more retail centers, apartment complexes, and public walkways along corridors like Main Street and E Cypress Road. When a property owner lets a spill, broken pavement, or poor lighting go unaddressed, someone can end up seriously hurt through no fault of their own. California law requires proving the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before your fall — which is why quick action to document the scene matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly; we're a free service that connects injured Oakley residents with an independent attorney who understands how local property and premises liability cases are built. If you were hurt on someone else's property, you can start by telling us what happened and let an attorney evaluate your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify evidence, like prior complaints or maintenance logs, that supports this before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last
items.desc: Many Oakley businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Your Own Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California is a pure comparative fault state, so even if you were partly responsible for the fall, you may still be able to recover a share of your damages.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in Oakley?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim notice. An attorney can tell you exactly which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell in a parking lot along Main Street or Empire Avenue and don't know who owns the property?
items.answer: That's common, especially with shopping centers that have multiple tenants and management companies. An attorney working with you can pull ownership and lease records to identify every responsible party before pursuing a claim.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You only pay if your case results in a settlement or award.
